subject: Archaeology
title: The Flores Hobbit: A Tiny Human
description: A fast breakdown of The Flores Hobbit: A Tiny Human for builders.

hook.text: On a remote Indonesian island, archaeologists found a human species that stood just three and a half feet tall.

buildup.text: Homo floresiensis was found in Liang Bua cave in 2003. They had small brains but made stone tools and hunted pygmy elephants.

discovery.text: They survived on Flores until at least 50,000 years ago — meaning they overlapped with modern humans in the region.

twist.text: Local legends describe small forest people called Ebu Gogo. Some wonder if folk memory preserved a real species.

climax.text: Island dwarfism explains their size — isolation on small islands shrinks large animals and can shrink humans too.

punchline.text: A real human species the size of a toddler hunted elephants on an island.

quiz.question: What likely explains the small size of Homo floresiensis?
options: They were children of a normal-sized species
Island dwarfism caused by long-term isolation on a small island
A genetic disease that stunted their growth

details.summary: Homo floresiensis, nicknamed the Hobbit, was a meter-tall hominin discovered on the Indonesian island of Flores in 2003. It survived until roughly 50,000 years ago, raising questions about island dwarfism in humans and the diversity of hominin species that coexisted with us.
details.whyItMatters: The Hobbit shocked researchers who assumed only Homo sapiens existed recently. It proved that multiple human species coexisted far more recently than anyone expected, challenging simple narratives of human evolution.
takeaways: Homo floresiensis stood about one meter tall on Flores island
It survived until roughly 50,000 years ago
Its discovery suggests island dwarfism affected hominins like other mammals

faq.question: Why was the Hobbit so small?
faq.answer: Island dwarfism is a well-known evolutionary phenomenon where large animals shrink on islands with limited resources. Elephants on Flores also dwarfed. Homo floresiensis likely descended from a larger hominin that shrank over generations of island isolation.

faq.question: Could the Hobbit just be a diseased modern human?
faq.answer: This was proposed early on, but multiple skeletons showing the same small stature and primitive features have ruled out individual pathology. The consistent body plan across multiple individuals confirms Homo floresiensis as a distinct species, not a diseased individual.
